code: scaled_l2 <- new_distance(   name = "scaled_l2_demo",   setup = function(X) {     scale <- apply(X, 2L, stats::sd)     scale[!is.finite(scale) | scale <= 0] <- 1     list(scale = scale)   },   eval_batch = function(X, X0, ctx) {     D <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(X0)), function(j) {       delta <- sweep(X, 2L, X0[j, ], "-")       sqrt(rowSums(sweep(delta, 2L, ctx$scale, "/")^2))     }, numeric(nrow(X)))     matrix(D, nrow = nrow(X), ncol = nrow(X0))   } )  X <- matrix(rnorm(80), 40, 2) X0 <- matrix(rnorm(12), 6, 2)  ctx_dist <- scaled_l2$setup(X) D <- distance_eval_batch(scaled_l2, X, X0, ctx = ctx_dist) dim(D) #> [1] 40  6

title: Nonparametric regression via TDNN rank weights — np_tdnn
text: data Optional data frame (tibble) containing covariates outcome column. Column names must non-missing, non-empty, unique. x_cols Names integer indices covariate columns data. y_col Name integer index outcome column data. y Optional numeric outcome vector length n. data-frame interface, use instead y_col. X Numeric matrix (n x p) matrix interface. Y Numeric outcome vector length n matrix interface. X0 Numeric matrix (m x p) target points; mutually exclusive x0. x0 Numeric vector length p single target point. distance Distance name specification (example "l2"). method One "exact" "asymp" TDNN rank weights. s1 Positive integer; smaller U-statistic order.  Must satisfy s1 < s2. s2 Positive integer; larger U-statistic order.  Must satisfy s1 < s2 <= n. dim Positive integer; localization dimension.  Defaults ncol(X) NULL. normalize Logical; renormalize asymptotic rank table sum 1 (used method = "asymp"; default TRUE). se Logical; compute delete-1 jackknife standard errors. jackknife One "fast", "loo", "none".  "fast" (default) uses prefix/suffix rank-order engine; "loo" recomputes leave-one-weights scratch; "none" skips SEs entirely. ctx Optional context passed distance rank-weight evaluators. return Optional extras addition always-returned mu, se, meta.  Allowed values: c("W", "ranks", "ord", "dx", "y", "ess", "neighbors"). neighbors extra returns nearest observation target; TDNN signed weight support.

title: Minimal PLQR demo data (oracle nuisances; no internal fitting) (experimental) — plqr_demo_data
text: Generates data partially linear quantile regression (PLQR) model $$   Q_{\tau}(Y \mid D, U) \;=\; D^{\top}\,\theta_{0} \;+\; g_{0}(U) \, , $$ user-chosen design nonparametric shape nuisance \(g_{0}\); demo specializes \(U = X\). title: Draw one sample from a named CATE simulation DGP — sim_cate_data
text: Six designs available: dgp1_linear Linear CATE \(\tau(x) = \beta'x\); logistic propensity. Correctly specified OLS-interaction benchmark. dgp2_nonlinear Sharpened nonlinear CATE \(\tau(x) = 0.5 + 0.75\sin(1.5 x_1)\); propensity. Default target interior point \(x_0 = (1,0,\ldots)\) local CATE visibly nonlinear around evaluation point. dgp3_sparse_overlap \(\tau\) DGP 2; propensity interpolates 0.5 x0 much sharper near-boundary logistic far x0, using tighter Gaussian overlap pocket. Default target interior point \(x_0 = (1,0,\ldots)\). dgp4_clustered \(\tau\) propensity DGP 2; covariates three-component mixture: 80\ x0) plus two diffuse 10\ \((4.5,2,0,\ldots)\) \((-2.5,-2,0,\ldots)\) covariance \(1.25^2 \). Observations independent draws mixture; name indicate clustered sampling. Default target \(x_0 = (1,0,\ldots)\) inner cluster recentered . dgp5_correlated Covariates \(X \sim N(0,\Sigma)\) \(\Sigma_{12} = \rho = 0.85\); \(\tau(x) = \sin(2x_1) + 0.5x_1^2\); evaluation point \(x_0 = (0.75, 0)\). dnn_oracle_mahal benchmark uses Mahalanobis distance account -diagonal covariance. dgp6_nuisance_efficiency Propensity \(e(x) = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}(1.25(x_1 - 1) - 0.75x_2)\) marginal regression \(m(x) = 1 + 1.5(x_1 - 1) - x_2\) aligned simple benchmark nuisance models, \(\tau(x) = 0.5 + 0.60\sin(1.5 x_1)\) remains nonlinear. Tests full-sample cross-fitted nuisance workflows. Default target \(x_0 = (1,0,\ldots)\).
